All of this is in `src/tessel/views.py`.

**Classes**
- `View` is the base class.
  - `View.to_view_func(name, *args, **kwargs)` (line 86) is a classmethod that returns a plain `view(**kwargs)` function. On each request it instantiates the class, or reuses one instance if `init_every_request` is `False`. It then calls `self.run_view(**kwargs)` through `active_app.ensure_sync`.
  - It copies `methods`, `provide_automatic_options` and `view_class` onto the function, and applies any `decorators`. The route registration (`app.attach_route_rule(...)`, per the docstring example) reads `view.methods` to decide which HTTP methods the route accepts.
- `VerbView(View)` (line 138) is the class that has `get()` and `post()`.
  - `__init_subclass__` (line 165) builds `cls.methods` at class-creation time. It inherits the bases' `methods`, then adds the upper-cased name of every verb in `http_method_funcs` that the class defines (`get` becomes `GET`, `post` becomes `POST`).
  - `run_view(**kwargs)` (line 182) does the per-request dispatch. It looks up `getattr(self, request.method.lower())` and calls it with the URL kwargs. `HEAD` falls back to `get` if there is no `head` handler.

**Flow:** `CounterAPI.to_view_func("counter")` returns the view function with `methods={"GET","POST"}`. The route is registered with those methods. A request creates the instance, `run_view` picks `get` or `post` from `request.method`, and the handler's response is returned.
